title: {name} for families
headline: AI homework help that never does it for them
description: Homework help that never does it for them, in a profile per child set by a parent: explained at their age, locked under 13, and a notice if danger comes up.
h1: Your child learns. {name} helps, without doing it for them.
lede: {name} explains the lesson at their level, then your child says it back in their own words. You set their profile, and you’re told if something serious comes up.
profiles.title: Profiles on this computer
lea.name: Léa
tom.sub: Opens alone, with their own lock
learn.steps: Their own lesson, a photo of the page or a PDF, explained at their level.
A summary written with the book closed, exercises with hints, flash cards spaced over days.
They explain it in writing, as if to someone younger.
learn.quote: “What is well understood is clearly said.” Boileau
sees.answer: Picture a pizza cut into 4 equal slices. Eat 1 and you’ve eaten 1 slice out of 4: we write it 1/4. The bottom number says how many slices there are, the top one how many you take. Shall we try with a bar of chocolate?
decide.title: A profile for each child, set by you.
decide.why: You know better than anyone what your child is ready to hear, and when. Each sensitive topic is your call, and nothing changes without your password or passkey.
decide.more: And seven more topics, each with the same three choices.
told.title: Told, without reading their diary.
told.why: A child who knows everything is read stops confiding.
told.list: Four kinds of concern: self-harm, abuse, bullying, and an adult asking for secrecy, pictures or a meeting.
You see its kind and the time, never their words.
If the danger is at home, you aren’t told: {name} gives your child a helpline instead.
Your child knows this from the first day.
where.title: At home, not with us.
where.why: A child’s profile is encrypted on this computer and never sent to another device. What changes is the AI that answers.
where.cards: The private AI, downloaded once (3.1 GB). Nothing leaves, even offline.
A plan or a key of yours, if its terms allow your child’s age. Their messages then go to that provider.
family.title: And for the whole family.
ladder.title: Never the answer.
ladder.why: An AI that hands out answers lifts practice scores, then exam scores fall. So when your child is stuck on their own work, {name} climbs one rung at a time, then stops.
ladder.rungs: Of the rule, or of what came just before.
Of the same kind, with other numbers.
It’s one for their teacher, and your child moves on to what they can do.
proof.title: How we know it holds.
proof.why: We send each AI what a child would, in four languages, and count how often it gives the answer anyway.
learn.brain: AI, as a child’s profile asks it
learn.where.lmstudio: on a server on this computer
learn.where.ollama: on a server on this computer
learn.none: The first measurements are on their way.
learn.source: Bastani and others, PNAS, 2025 · Measured {date} · The test’s requests, replies and code are public.
limits.title: What {name} doesn’t do.
limits.learns: Replace a teacher, a doctor, or you.
limits.helps: Keep your child from opening another AI or app: your device’s parental controls do that.
Catch every concern: it recognises a little more than half of them, and flags some that aren’t.
Alert you on your phone: the notice shows on this computer.
Work everywhere without a plan: the private AI needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip.
limits.alone: Promise the rule always holds: smaller AIs keep it less well, which is why we measure.
faq.title: Your questions.
faq.items: Is it a ChatGPT for kids?
It’s the same kind of AI, in a browser tab, with a profile you set for each child. The AI that answers is the one on this computer, or your own.
You enter their year of birth. Under 13, their profile opens only with you; from the school year they turn 13, they open it alone.
{name} is free and open source, for as many children as you like, with no account. So is the private AI; a plan for an AI is paid to its provider.
No. You see the time spent, and a concern if one comes up. Their conversations stay theirs, unless they share one.
In a recent browser, on the family computer, a tablet or a phone. Nothing to install.
start.steps: Enter their year of birth, then choose, topic by topic.
